deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a space stratified by a poset I. X_i^* is the stratum indexed by i, X_i is its closure, and X_i ⊂ X_j implies i ≤ j. From the previous pages: for i ≤ j, V_{i,j} is a (germ of a) tubular neighbourhood of X_i^* inside X_j. V*_{i,j} = V_{i,j} ∩ X_j^* is the deleted neighbourhood, the part of the tube lying in the open stratum X_j^*. It is open in V_{i,j}. The previous page decided to work mainly with the X_i^* and the 'elementary' pieces V_{i,j}, V*_{i,j}.

On this page Grothendieck bundles these pieces into simplicially indexed coproducts:
- (14) V_{Δ1} = ∐_{i≤j} V_{i,j}, and V*_{Δ1} = ∐_{i≤j} V*_{i,j}, an open subset of V_{Δ1}.
- Here Δ0 = I and Δ1 = {(i,j) : i ≤ j}. These are the 0- and 1-simplices of the nerve of I (degenerate ones included).
- X*_{Δ0} denotes ∐_i X_i^*.

(15) is the 'sum' diagram:
- V*_{Δ1} ↪ V_{Δ1} ← X*_{Δ0} (the second map is the zero-sections X_i^* → V_{i,j});
- V*_{Δ1} → X*_{Δ0} (inclusion V*_{i,j} ⊂ X_j^*);
- dotted maps to X.

(15) is the coproduct of the elementary diagrams (17), one for each pair i ≤ j:
- V*_{i,j} → V_{i,j} ← X_i^*;
- V*_{i,j} → X_j^*;
- dotted maps of V_{i,j}, X_i^* and X_j^* into X.

The source and target maps Δ1 → Δ0 appear as the two ways X*_{Δ0} receives data: through the zero-section (source i) and through the deleted tube (target j).

Grothendieck then doubts that notation (14) is useful. The square in (15) will in any case have to be considered from the viewpoint of a cocartesian square (pushout/gluing). The full-line diagram, being merely a 'sum', does not by itself encode how X is glued. The next page continues: X should be recovered, perhaps up to homeomorphism, by gluing, and the inclusion relations among the germs U^j_{i,h} are analysed.

The marginal NB seems to describe the shape of the indexing diagram (points with arrows) as a quiver/category generated by a graph. This would be the combinatorial shape (a subdivision/twisted-arrow-type category of I) over which the gluing diagram lives.

Purpose: a 'dévissage' of a tame stratified space into elementary pieces (strata, tubes, deleted tubes) plus a gluing diagram from which X is reconstructed. This is the programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: No real error. Minor point: for i = j the pieces degenerate (V_{i,i} and V*_{i,i} should both be X_i^*), so including the diagonal i ≤ j is a convention. Grothendieck does not spell this out.
As he himself notes, the coproduct (15) loses the gluing information, so it cannot by itself recover X. A colimit over the appropriate indexing category, not over a sum, is needed.

ideas.what: Decomposing a stratified space into strata X_i^*, tubular neighbourhoods V_{i,j} and deleted tubes V*_{i,j}, with zero-section and inclusion maps, as the elementary 'pieces'
ideas.modern_name: Tubular neighbourhood / link data of a stratified space (Thom–Mather control data, Quinn homotopy links)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (1969-70); Quinn (1988) for homotopy links
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (dévissage of stratified structures, tubes)

ideas.what: Indexing the pieces by the nerve of the stratification poset (Δ0 = I, Δ1 = pairs i ≤ j) and assembling them into a simplicially indexed diagram
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/colimit presentation of a stratified space over (a subdivision of) the nerve of the poset; cf. exit-path ∞-category, basics of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra App. A, 2009-17); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017); Treumann (2009)

ideas.what: Recognising that X should be recovered via a cocartesian (pushout) square rather than a sum diagram
ideas.modern_name: Recovering a stratified space as a (homotopy) pushout of tube and complement

missed.claim: An attempt to present a stratified space as a colimit of a diagram of strata, tubes and deleted tubes indexed by the simplices of the nerve of the stratification poset. This anticipates in spirit the later description of stratified spaces via exit-path categories / link data over sd(I). Here it is only begun, and Grothendieck questions his own notation.
missed.quote: je ne suis pas sûr que les notations (14) soient bien utiles - il faudra de toute façon le carré dans (15) ... cocartésien
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest: it shows Grothendieck around 1981+ heading toward a combinatorial (poset-nerve-indexed) gluing description of tame stratified spaces. This is close to modern reconstruction theorems (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Douteau–Waas). Mathematically it is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished working detail of the Esquisse §5 dévissage programme. The nerve-indexed organisation is suggestive but rudimentary and self-doubted, and the content is standard in the later literature.
transcription_corrections: The second diagram is labelled (17), not (16); the page skips (16), as the image shows.
In (15) the lower-left entry was first written V and corrected to X*_{Δ0}; a crossed-out line below the diagram reads roughly 'V_{Δ1} ← X*_{Δ0}'.

Bottom lines read roughly: 'Finalement, je ne suis pas sûr que les notations (14) soient bien utiles — il faudra de toute façon le carré dans (15) mis en vue du cocartésien[?], car le diagramme en traits pleins, qui est le diagramme "somme"'.
Margin note: 'NB Le genre[?] de diagramme ... engendré par ...', with a small drawing of points and arrows; the word read as 'carquois' is uncertain.
